mainTopic: Unclear wording in a שכיב מרע gift, a שכיב מרע who sold all his property, and a שכיב מרע who admits to owing money (the story of איסור גיורא)
overview: This amud opens with four unclear phrases a שכיב מרע (a person on his deathbed) might use when giving away property, such as 'he shall benefit from them' or 'he shall lean on them.' The גמרא asks whether each one makes a full gift and ends with תיקו, meaning no answer is found. Next it asks about a שכיב מרע who sold all his property and then recovered. Two reports in the name of רב seem to contradict each other. The גמרא settles them: if the sale money is still with him, he can retract, but if he used it to pay a debt, he cannot. Then it asks whether a שכיב מרע's admission (הודאה) that he owes money works. To answer, it tells the story of איסור the convert, whose 12,000 זוזים were held by רבא. רבא argues that איסור's son רב מרי cannot get the money by inheritance, by deathbed gift, or by any normal קנין. רב איקא points out that איסור could simply admit the money belongs to רב מרי. An admission document then comes out, and רבא complains about his loss. This proves that a שכיב מרע's admission is valid.

steps.title: What does 'he shall benefit from them' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a שכיב מרע who says 'so-and-so shall benefit from my property' is giving him all of it or only some benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'he shall benefit from them,' what is the law? Does he mean that all of it is a gift, or does he mean the person should get some benefit from it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what a dying person meant when he said someone 'shall benefit' from his property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words can be read two ways. One reading is a full gift of everything. The other is a small benefit, while the property itself stays with someone else. The question is how wide the gift is.

phrases.english: "He shall benefit from them," what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the dying man's property. He is talking about who gets it after him.

phrases.english: Is he saying that all of it shall be a gift,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא לִיתְהֲנֵי מִינַּיְיהוּ מִידֵּי קָאָמַר?
phrases.english: or perhaps he is saying he should get some benefit from them?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'יהנה בהן' give the whole property as a gift or only some benefit from it?

steps.title: More unclear phrases: 'be seen,' 'stand,' 'rely'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same kind of question about three more phrases a שכיב מרע might use.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He shall be seen in them,' what is the law? 'He shall stand in them,' what is the law? 'He shall lean on them,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds three more unclear expressions and asks what each one means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase hints that the person gets some connection to the property. None of them clearly says 'it is yours.' So the same doubt applies: a full gift, or something less?

keyTerms.meaning: He shall be seen in them

phrases.english: "He shall be seen in them," what is the law?
"He shall stand in them," what is the law?
"He shall lean on them," what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the same question to similar phrases
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do these phrases give a full gift or only partial use?

steps.title: The questions stay unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends all four questions with תיקו: no answer is found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it cannot answer these questions and leaves them open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means the doubt is never settled. In money matters, an unsettled doubt usually means the money stays with whoever already holds it. Here that is the heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question stays unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: All four unclear phrases ('benefit,' 'be seen,' 'stand,' 'lean') end in תיקו. The גמרא never decides whether they make a full gift.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The meaning of these phrases stays in doubt.

steps.title: A deathbed sale of all his property
steps.stepSummary: A new question: what is the law if a שכיב מרע sold all his property?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if he sold all his property, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a dying man who sold, rather than gave away, all he owned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if a שכיב מרע gives away all his property and then recovers, he can take the gift back. The question is whether a sale works the same way, since in a sale he got money in return.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:
If he sold all his property, what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'He' is still the שכיב מרע. The real question is what happens if he gets better.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מָכַר כׇּל נְכָסָיו, מַהוּ?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If a שכיב מרע who sold everything recovers, can he cancel the sale?

steps.title: רב: if he recovers, he cannot retract
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports in the name of רב that if the seller recovers, he cannot take back the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: if he recovered, he does not go back on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a first answer: the sale stands even if he recovers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sale is a real exchange: he got money for his land. So it is not like a deathbed gift, which depends on the man actually dying.

keyTerms.meaning: If he recovered (literally, 'if he stood up')

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
If he recovered, he cannot retract.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אִם עָמַד אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sale stands; he cannot retract.

steps.title: A second report from רב says the opposite
steps.stepSummary: At other times רב יהודה reported in the name of רב that the seller can retract, which seems to contradict the first report.
steps.simpleTranslation: And sometimes רב יהודה said in the name of רב: if he recovered, he can go back on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows a second version of רב's ruling that says the opposite of the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody asks a question out loud here. Still, two opposite reports from the same rabbi in the same chain create a contradiction, and the גמרא must explain it.

phrases.aramaic: וְזִימְנִין אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And at other times Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
If he recovered, he can retract.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזִימְנִין אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the seller cannot retract
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same rabbi is quoted as saying both 'cannot retract' and 'can retract.'

steps.title: No contradiction: it depends on the money
steps.stepSummary: The two rulings cover different cases. If the sale money is still with him, he can retract. If he used it to pay a debt, he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not argue. This one is where the coins are still there as they were; that one is where he used them to pay his debt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by giving each ruling its own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the coins are untouched, it looks as if he sold only because he expected to die. He never really needed the money, so he can undo the sale. If he paid a debt with it, the sale had a real purpose, so it stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He paid them toward his debt

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the pairing. 'Can retract' goes with the money still being there. 'Cannot retract' goes with the money already used to pay a debt.
steps.whatToRemember: A שכיב מרע who sold everything and recovered can cancel the sale only if the sale money is still sitting with him untouched.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
This one is where the coins still exist as they were,
phrases.notes: This goes with the ruling that he can retract, from step 6.

phrases.english: that one is where he paid them toward his debt.
phrases.notes: This goes with the ruling that he cannot retract, from step 5.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב gave two opposite rulings about the same case
steps.terutzMaskana: Retracting depends on whether the sale money is still with him or was used to pay a debt

steps.title: A deathbed admission
steps.stepSummary: New question: what is the law if a שכיב מרע admits that he owes someone money?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: a שכיב מרע who admitted (that money belongs to someone), what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a dying man's admission that he owes money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe he really owes the money. Or maybe he is just using an 'admission' as a way to give a gift. The question is whether such an admission works, and how.

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:
A dying person who admitted (owing money), what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: שְׁכִיב מְרַע שֶׁהוֹדָה, מַהוּ?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a שכיב מרע's admission of owing money valid?

steps.title: The story of איסור the convert begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a proof story: איסור the convert had 12,000 זוזים held by רבא. His son רב מרי was conceived before איסור converted and born after, and he was away learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: איסור the convert had twelve thousand זוזים at רבא's house. His son רב מרי was conceived not in holiness but born in holiness, and he was in the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts telling a story that it will use to answer the question. This step only sets up the facts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key fact is that רב מרי was conceived before his father converted. That means he is not his father's legal heir. The proof itself comes later, as the story goes on.

keyTerms.meaning: In holiness, meaning after the father became Jewish

steps.confusionAlert: רב מרי is a full Jew, since he was born after the conversion. He is still not his father's heir, because he was conceived before the conversion.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
For Issur the convert had
twelve thousand zuz at the house of Rava.
Rav Mari his son —
his conception was not in holiness,
phrases.notes: He was conceived while his father was not yet Jewish.

phrases.english: but his birth was in holiness;
and he was in the study hall.
phrases.notes: He was away when his father was dying, so he couldn't take the money himself.

steps.raayaObject: Whether a שכיב מרע's admission works
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of איסור the convert and his son רב מרי

steps.title: רבא: רב מרי can't get the money by inheritance or by gift
steps.stepSummary: רבא reasons that רב מרי cannot inherit, since he is not a legal heir. He also cannot get the money as a deathbed gift, because חכמים treated a deathbed gift like inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: how could רב מרי acquire this money? By inheritance? He is not an heir. By gift? חכמים made a deathbed gift like inheritance. Wherever inheritance works, a gift works, and wherever inheritance doesn't work, a gift doesn't work.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why he thinks רב מרי has no way to get his father's money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inheritance fails because רב מרי is not a legal heir. A deathbed gift is made without a formal act of acquiring (קנין), and חכמים gave it this power by treating it like inheritance. So it works only where inheritance would work. This blocks the gift route too, and sets up the question of what other route might work.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who is a legal heir

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the general rule that a deathbed gift is tied to inheritance. That rule is the reason the story will need a different route, apparently an admission, to give רב מרי the money.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכִי נִיקְנִינְהוּ רַב מָרִי לְהָנֵי זוּזֵי?
phrases.english: How could Rav Mari acquire these coins?
If by inheritance —
he is not fit to inherit.
If by gift —

phrases.aramaic: מַתְּנַת שְׁכִיב מְרַע כִּירוּשָּׁה שַׁוְּיוּהָ רַבָּנַן;
phrases.english: the Sages made the gift of a dying person like inheritance;
anywhere that inheritance applies —
a gift applies,
anywhere that inheritance does not apply —
a gift does not apply.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הֵיכִי נִיקְנִינְהוּ רַב מָרִי לְהָנֵי זוּזֵי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with רבא's reasoning about the facts just given
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A deathbed gift works only where inheritance would work, so רב מרי cannot receive his father's money by inheritance or by gift.

steps.title: רבא shows every normal way of transferring the money fails
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues his reasoning. He goes through משיכה, חליפין, אגב קרקע and מעמד שלשתן, and shows that none of them can get the money to רב מרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If by pulling, the money is not with him. If by symbolic exchange, coins cannot be acquired by exchange. If along with land, he has no land. If by having all three present, if he sends for me, I won't go.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא keeps building his case from step 10. He checks every normal way to transfer the money and shows why each one fails, so he thinks the money stays with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inheritance and a deathbed gift were already ruled out. Now רבא blocks every regular קנין too. Coins cannot be pulled because they are not there, חליפין does not work on coins, איסור owns no land to attach them to, and מעמד שלשתן needs רבא himself to show up, which he refuses to do.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling: acquiring an object by drawing it into your possession
Symbolic exchange: acquiring by handing over an item such as a cloth
Along with land: movable items acquired together with a piece of land
In the presence of all three: the giver, the receiver, and the person holding the item

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying these methods never work. He is saying that in this specific situation each one is blocked.

phrases.english: If by pulling – they are not with him.
If by symbolic exchange –
a coin cannot be acquired by symbolic exchange.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַגַּב קַרְקַע – לֵית לֵיהּ אַרְעָא.
phrases.english: If along with land – he has no land.
If in the presence of all three –
phrases.notes: The three are איסור the giver, רב מרי the receiver, and רבא, who is holding the money.

phrases.english: if he sends for me, I won't go.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's reasoning from step 10, moving from inheritance and gift to the regular קנינים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every standard method of transferring the money to רב מרי is blocked, so the money stays with רבא.

steps.title: רב איקא asks why איסור cannot just admit the money is רב מרי's
steps.stepSummary: רב איקא בריה דרב אמי challenges רבא: איסור could admit that the money belongs to רב מרי, and רב מרי would acquire it through that admission.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב איקא son of רב אמי objected: Why? Let איסור admit that these זוזים belong to רב מרי, and let him acquire them through the admission!
steps.whatsHappening: רב איקא pokes a hole in רבא's list. He points out a way רבא left out: a simple admission by איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An admission is not a קנין at all. It is a statement that the money already belongs to someone else. So none of the blocks רבא listed apply to it, and רב מרי could get the money that way.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it: introduces a challenge
An admission, often a written document of admission

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אִיקָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rav Ika son of Rav Ami objected to this:
Why?
Let Isur admit
that these zuz belong to Rav Mari,
and let him acquire them through the admission!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אִיקָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's claim in step 11 that no method could work.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's conclusion that no method could transfer the money to רב מרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An admission does not need pulling, exchange, land, or רבא's presence, so it gets around every block רבא listed.

steps.title: An admission document appears and רבא loses the money
steps.stepSummary: A written admission comes out of איסור's house. רבא is annoyed that people are teaching litigants claims and causing him a loss. This shows the admission of a שכיב מרע works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, a written admission came out of איסור's house. רבא got angry and said: They are teaching people claims and making me lose.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: איסור actually makes the admission, and רבא admits it cost him the money. This answers the question from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's complaint that he is losing the money shows he accepted that the admission works. So a שכיב מרע's admission that he owes someone money is valid, even when a gift would not be.
steps.whatToRemember: A שכיב מרע's admission (הודאה) transfers the money, even where inheritance, a deathbed gift, and every normal קנין would not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the question raised in step 8: when a שכיב מרע admits he owes money, the admission works.

phrases.english: In the meantime, an admission document came out of Isur's house.
Rava became angry and said:
They are teaching people claims,
phrases.notes: He means people like רב איקא, whose idea of an admission reached איסור.

phrases.english: and causing me a loss.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows in practice that רב איקא's suggestion from step 12 worked, which completes the proof story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A שכיב מרע's admission is valid and transfers ownership, as shown by רבא losing איסור's money.
